behavioral_concerns: follow up: A fenced or commented pseudo `## Performance Targets` heading is ignored by target parsing but still treated as a declaration during policy validation, causing a false `performance policy mismatch` when performance policy is disabled.

evidence.summary: Bounded inspection confirmed that markdownHeadingPresent returns true for any trimmed matching heading line, including lines inside fences or multiline HTML comments; ParsePerformanceTargets applies exclusions for those constructs [qa-v1-block-9c5f43b294578fed6796f5b9].

theories.claim: A fenced or HTML-commented `## Performance Targets` pseudo-heading causes disabled-policy requirements validation to emit a false `performance policy mismatch`, even though target parsing ignores that pseudo-section.
theories.basis: ValidateRequirementsContentWithPolicy uses a separate heading-presence check for policy enforcement, while ParsePerformanceTargets explicitly ignores fenced and commented pseudo-sections [qa-v1-block-3cceb141b86f4e4c3b8609e8, qa-v1-block-9c5f43b294578fed6796f5b9, qa-v1-block-e119c25baa75d6da3419c82e].
theories.confirmation_condition: With disabled performance policy, requirements containing `## Performance Targets` only inside a fenced block or HTML comment produce a `performance policy mismatch` while ParsePerformanceTargets returns no targets or findings.
theories.refutation_condition: The declaration check applies the same fence, comment, quote, and indentation exclusions as ParsePerformanceTargets, so pseudo-headings do not produce a policy mismatch.
theories.inconclusive_condition: The implementation of markdownHeadingPresent or its interaction with validation cannot be inspected.
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: Statically compare pseudo-section handling in ParsePerformanceTargets with markdownHeadingPresent and inspect existing table-driven tests without executing or mutating the repository.
